key_insight: Splat2Act personalizes a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policy to a specific home or office using captured scene data, avoiding the need for expensive in-environment demonstrations. It bridges the gap between generalist manipulation policies and real-world deployment in user-specific spaces.
problem_solved: Generalist robot manipulation policies can fail completely in new, personalized environments because they do not know the layout, objects, and geometry of each user’s space. Collecting real demonstrations for every deployment scene is costly and impractical.
method: Capture the target environment and build a scene representation for simulation.
Use an automated real-to-sim-to-real pipeline to adapt a pretrained VLA policy to the user’s specific setting.
Transfer the personalized policy back to the real world for manipulation tasks like picking up objects from shelves, counters, and tables.
impact: This approach makes it more practical to deploy generalist robot policies in everyday environments without collecting large amounts of robot data on-site. For practitioners, it offers a scalable path toward personalized robot manipulation in homes and offices.
